summary: Read a binary tree. Find the largest count of nodes on a route that starts at the root and stops at a leaf. That count is the height. A tree holding only the root has height one. A tree holding no node at all has height zero. A leaf is a node that no longer has a child. Write the height as one integer. Numbers stored in nodes may include 20. While measuring height, count nodes only and do not read those numbers.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is a level-order node count, using a dot for a missing child.
